:: JUDGMENT :
:

The Halasur Police Station, Bengaluru filed this charge sheet against the accused No.1 & 2 for the offence punishable under Sections 120(B), 420, 471, 468 R/w. 34 of IPC.
2.

The brief facts of the prosecution case that:
That, accused no.1 and CW1 are siblings.
With regard to their family property at No.13 situated at Magarath Road, Bengaluru, accused No.1 was given the GPA by CW1 to manage the said property.
However, doubting his intentions, the GPA was canceled and a notice was also sent in this regard.

However, accused hatched a conspiracy to cheat CW1 & dishonestly created forged sale deeds even though GPA was canceled and accused No.1 fraudulently used the said created and forged seven sale deeds as genuine documents knowing that at the time when he used it to be forged documents and accused No.1 created false sale deeds and used the same with an intention to cheat CW1 and thereby accused No.1 cheated CW.1 and committed the Hulsoor Ps vs S. Jagadish on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139933427/
1 offence punishable u/S.120(B), 420, 471, 468 R/w. 34 of IPC.
3.
The Investigating officer after completion of the investigation, filed the charge-sheet against the accused No. 1 & 2.
This Court took cognizance for the said offence and registered the case and issued summons to the accused.
Accused No.1 appeared through his advocate and got enlarged on bail.
Case against accused No.2 ordered discharged.
4. After compliance of Section 207 of Cr.P.C., this Court framed charge against the accused No.1 and read over the same to him in the language known to him.
The accused No.1 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Therefore, the case was posted for trial.
5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1, the prosecution got examined one witnesses as PW1 and got marked five documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 and closed its side.
6. As the witness/victim turned hostile, the remaining witnesses were dropped and the statement of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.

7. Heard the learned A.P.P. and learned counsel for the accused No. 1.
8.

The points that arise for my consideration are as under :-
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, accused No.1 hatched a conspiracy to cheat CW1 & created forged sale deed pertaining to property No.13 situated at Magarath Road even though CW1 had canceled the GPA and accused No.1 fraudulently used the said created and forged seven sale deeds as genuine documents knowing that at the time when used it to be a forged documents and accused No.1 created the false sale deeds and used the same with an intention cheated CW1 and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sections 120(B),
420, 471, 468 R/w. 34 of IPC?
2. What order?

9. My findings on the above said points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative.
 Point No.2 : As per the final order for  the following:
 REASONS 10. POINT No.1:- It is the case of the prosecution that, accused No.1 hatched a conspiracy to cheat CW1 of the family property at No.13 situated at Magarath Road and created forged sale deeds even though GPA was canceled by CW1 and accused No.1 fraudulently used the said created and forged Hulsoor Ps vs S. Jagadish on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139933427/
2 seven sale deeds as genuine documents with an intention to cheat CW1 and thereby accused No. 1 cheated CW1.
11.
CW1- Hemalatha is examined as PW1.
She deposed that, accused is her bother.
Earlier there was a civil dispute between her and accused.
They both compromised the same.
PW1 further deposed that, accused did not she filed this complaint as per Ex.P1 against the accused out of misunderstanding.
Accused did not cheated her.
Though PW1 identified her signature on Ex.P1 & 2.
She deposed that, she does not know the contents of those documents.
Though she was treated as hostile by the prosecution nothing was elicited in her cross-examination.

12. On perusal, the prosecution had to prove that, accused No.1 furtherance of common intention,
hatched a conspiracy with an intention to cheat CW1 & cheated CW-1 by dishonestly registering the property No.13 situated at Magarath Road by creating forged sale deeds even though GPA was canceled and accused No.1 fraudulently used the said created and forged seven sale deeds as genuine document knowing that at the time when used it to be a forged document and accused No.1 created the false sale deeds and used the same with an intention to cheat CW1 and thereby accused No. 1 cheated CW1.
13.
As the victim/informant and the supporting witnesses turned hostile, there is no iota of evidence to attract the offence alleged by the prosecution.
As such examination of the prosecution witnesses only for the purpose of completing the procedural aspect will not serve any judicious purpose and is sheer waste of the precious time of the Court.

At this stage, it is relevant to rely upon the decision of Satish Mehra v. Delhi Administration and Another, (1996) 9 SCC 766, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as follows:
"When the judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the conclusion on the future date."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. The principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above case is applicable to this case as well.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, it is clear that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts.
Under these facts and circumstances of the case, the Point No.1 is answered in the negative.

15. POINT No.2:- In view of my discussions on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
:O R D E R:
Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the Accused is acquitted for the offence punishable under Sections 120(B), 420, 471, 468 R/w. 34 of IPC.
The bail bond of the accused stands canceled.
Cash security to be refunded after three months.
